## Highlights
Showing the 12 most recent highlights from 16 user-facing changes.
### New
- A tab playing sound shows a speaker badge on its icon, which mutes or unmutes it, and bars behind its title that follow its sound on Chromium pages. Tabs taking part in tab sharing show a badge that goes to the other tab or stops sharing. Look and Feel can show the status in place of the tab’s icon, or turn the bars off. - On Mac, coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex can use Crest as their browser in the Spaces you choose: open and read tabs, click and type, take screenshots, and read a page’s console and network requests. Turn it on in Settings › Agents. Crest asks before each new agent connects, and every tab an agent uses shows its badge.
### Improved
- A Space’s Search with menu shows each provider’s icon, like the default search menu. - Each section in Settings has its own color, drawn from the Space templates.
### Fixed
- Buttons in the floating sidebar respond to taps, and its Settings button opens Settings. - Settings on iPhone and iPad shows Crest’s real app icon, including the one you chose, in light and dark. - On iPhone and iPad, General settings shows whether Crest is your default browser instead of Unavailable when iOS limits how often Crest can check. - Edit Shortcuts and Add Provider in Search settings open right away on iPhone and iPad. - On iPhone, Show Full History in a page’s Back and Forward menus opens History. - On iPhone, Crest asks before downloading a risky file from the page you’re viewing, instead of leaving the download waiting for approval. - While a Peek is open, Copy Link, Share, Find, Zoom, Reload, Back, Forward, Print, Export as PDF and Save Web Archive act on the page in the Peek instead of the tab behind it, and Close Tab closes the Peek. - Command-G and Command-Shift-G move to the next and previous find-in-page match, and reopen the find bar with your last search.

## Highlights
### Fixed
- Crest windows on Mac no longer keep the system's WindowServer busy, which could use a lot of CPU on large or high-refresh external displays. The focused-window transparency setting has been removed.
---
Stable releases are signed, notarized, and ready for everyday use.

## Highlights
### New
- A new General setting keeps the developer toolbar from opening by itself on local pages. Shift-Command-I still shows it on any page.
### Improved
- Drag the frame around a page on any edge to move the window, as you can from the sidebar. The gap around a floating sidebar moves the window too. Borderless windows have no frame, so every click still reaches the page.
### Fixed
- Full-screen videos in the Chromium engine hide the pointer when you stop moving it, as they do in WebKit. - A page you send from a Quick Window to another Space responds to clicks and typing as soon as it appears, instead of only after you switch tabs. - A hidden sidebar slides out at the window's edge only when that window is in front. Moving the pointer over a window in the background no longer opens its sidebar and leaves it stuck open. - Screen sharing works in Slack huddles and in Slack's call test on pages that run in Chromium. As in Chrome, a site can ask to share your screen without a click of its own, and macOS still asks what to share. - Tabs take the title a page gives itself after it finishes loading. A link you open in the background with Command-click, or a page that shows “Loading…” first, no longer stays named by its address or placeholder. - Pages in Chromium that have no title of their own show the site’s name, as WebKit pages do, instead of their full address. A Chromium tab that reloads in the background keeps its title.
